# Encryption and decryption programs

	These are 2 programs, one encrypts and the other decrypts


# Ready to start

(find a way to get encrypt.c, decrypt.c and libec.h)

```console
$ make all
```

In this logic of encryption, there is a notion of golden numbers, wich are:
- NB_BYTES=4                // This number corresponds to length of one information
- REDUNDANT_BYTES=8         // This number represent the number of times the information will be repeated
- NB_KEY=15                 // This number corresponds to the power of randomness in front of repeated the characters
- SEEDKEY="Toy-case-exempl" // This "number" could be better considered as a string that will differentiate each compiled program

The Makefile are editable so the golden numbers could be modify.

## Strongest configuration:

It is possible to increase _PUI\_ENCRYPT_, _NB\_CLEF_ but this number is complitely enought !

- NB_OCTET   =4
- PUI_ENCRYPT=10
- NB_CLEF    =100


## Worst configuration:

The number of bytes it's not enought to differentiate all the ASCII carracter stored.

- NB_OCTET   =1
- PUI_ENCRYPT=2
- NB_CLEF    =1

  
## To accept a certain wrong bit

Set this value as you want:

- EPSILON=0.75

It's a ratio like SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio) to gets a certain tolerance on bytes errors received.

# How to use it

```console
$ ./encrypt Hello world (press Crtl-D to escape)
$ > 
$ 
$ decrypt (Paste the whole message above)
$ > Hello world
```

This is done with this combination of parameters:
- NBO      = NB_BYTES=4
- REDBYTES = REDUNDANT_BYTES=8
- NBK      = NB_KEY=15
- SKEY     = SEEDKEY="Toy-case-exempl"

## Beter utilisation

```console
$ ./encrypt > code
$ ./encrypt Hello world > code.txt
$ ./decrypt < code
$ > Hello world
```

## Best utilisation

```console
$ ./encrypt < encrypt.c > code
$ ./decrypt < code
$ > ...
```


## To get it anywhere

```sh
$ sudo cp encrypt /bin
$ sudo cp decrypt /bin
```


## Limite and power

### Here is the stress test of repetition:


To do so I encrypted 64 'a' like so:

```console
$ ./encrypt aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
```

#### Test no°1

This is done by this combination of parameters:
- NBO    = NB_OCTET=1
- PUIENC = PUI_ENCRYPT=8
- NBC    = NB_CLEF=10

The results:

[![1 byte 8 times redondant with 10 different keys](./picture/1oct-8pow-10key.png)](/picture)

We can see at the end of the message a pattern repeating itself. This is expected because there is only 10 keys for 64 repeted letters.
We can also see that it repeats roughly 6 times and this represent 64 divided by 10.

#### Test no°2

This is done by this combination of parameters:
- NBO    = NB_OCTET=8
- PUIENC = PUI_ENCRYPT=1
- NBC    = NB_CLEF=10

The results:

[![8 bytes 1 times redondant with 10 different keys](./picture/8oct-1pow-10key.png)](/picture)

We roughly see the same thing as above, except that the scale of the vertical axis is much greater than previously and this is due to the numbers of bytes on wich the information is encoded
